headline: Apple's camera-equipped AirPods demoed in macOS beta
summary: A leaked video from the latest macOS beta shows AirPods using 'Visual Intelligence' to identify objects and potentially assist AI features.
details: A short video clip discovered within the macOS Tahoe 26.7 Release Candidate offers a potential first look at Apple's rumored camera-equipped AirPods.
The demo features a user wearing the new AirPods, holding up a book, while a Siri voice-over explains 'Visual Intelligence' can 'save' what the wearer sees.

Bloomberg's Mark Gurman previously reported these AirPods could use low-resolution visual information to act as 'eyes' for AI features, enabling tasks like turn-by-turn directions or answering questions about surroundings.
The AirPods in the clip appear slightly thicker than AirPods Pro 3, with longer stems to accommodate cameras, though no LED indicators are visible from the back angle shown.
While not designed for taking photos or videos, the stealthy form factor of these camera-equipped AirPods could raise privacy concerns, similar to those faced by Meta's Ray-Ban smart glasses.
If demo videos are appearing in OS betas, the AirPods with cameras may launch alongside an improved Siri in September, coinciding with the next iPhone generation.
caption:
Apple's rumored camera-equipped AirPods have been spotted in a leaked video from the latest macOS beta, showcasing 'Visual Intelligence' capabilities.

A short video clip discovered within the macOS Tahoe 26.7 Release Candidate offers a potential first look at Apple's rumored camera-equipped AirPods.

The demo features a user wearing the new AirPods, holding up a book, while a Siri voice-over explains 'Visual Intelligence' can 'save' what the wearer sees.

Bloomberg's Mark Gurman previously reported these AirPods could use low-resolution visual information to act as 'eyes' for AI features, enabling tasks like turn-by-turn directions or answering questions about surroundings.

The AirPods in the clip appear slightly thicker than AirPods Pro 3, with longer stems to accommodate cameras, though no LED indicators are visible from the back angle shown.

While not designed for taking photos or videos, the stealthy form factor of these camera-equipped AirPods could raise privacy concerns, similar to those faced by Meta's Ray-Ban smart glasses.

If demo videos are appearing in OS betas, the AirPods with cameras may launch alongside an improved Siri in September, coinciding with the next iPhone generation.

headline: Nvidia CMP 170HX GPUs hacked to unlock 64GB VRAM from 8GB
summary: A software mod boosts the memory capacity of Nvidia's cryptocurrency mining GPUs by up to 8X, turning old crypto hardware into potential AI accelerators.
details: Modders have found a way to unlock previously inaccessible VRAM on Nvidia's CMP 170HX graphics cards using a software-only solution called CMP Unlocker. This exploit can boost the memory from 8GB to 64GB, or from 10GB to 40GB, making these repurposed mining GPUs more viable for AI tasks.

The CMP 170HX is based on the GA100 Ampere silicon, the same chip used in Nvidia's A100 accelerator. While the GA100 chip physically contains six HBM2e memory stacks, Nvidia disabled some of these in the CMP 170HX for product segmentation and to use binned silicon.

The exploit bypasses Nvidia's security measures, effectively 'downloading more memory' without any physical modifications. However, the success and stability of the unlocked memory depend on the silicon lottery, as it's unclear if Nvidia disabled the memory due to defects or for segmentation.

Beyond memory, the software mod also restores some of the card's computational performance and upgrades its PCIe interface speed from PCIe 1.0 x4 to PCIe 2.0 x4. Further performance gains are possible with physical modifications, such as soldering missing capacitors to enable full PCIe x16 bandwidth.

Originally priced at $4,300, CMP 170HX cards now sell for around $250 on eBay. Following news of the exploit, prices have surged to over $1,000, making these cards a more attractive, albeit risky, option for AI users seeking high memory capacity at a lower cost than enterprise-grade accelerators like the A100.
